title: mZN Staining Protocol
author: Asar Khan
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.r4xd8xn

steps.title: Prepare Stool Smear
steps.instruction: Spread the stool sample evenly on the middle of the slide using a constant rotational movement for 5 to 10 minutes.

steps.title: Air-Dry the Slide
steps.instruction: Place the slides on a dryer with the smeared surface facing upwards and allow to air-dry for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Fix the Smear
steps.instruction: Fix the dried smear using absolute methanol for 3-5 minutes.

steps.title: Apply Carbol-fuchsine Stain
steps.instruction: Cover the entire smear by adding Carbol-fuchsine solution and let it sit for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Wash the Slide
steps.instruction: Gently wash the slide with tap water using a dropper to avoid exposing the slide to high water pressure.

steps.title: Decolorize the Smear
steps.instruction: Apply 4-6 drops of decolorizer (Acid Alcohol) to the smear, then wash the slide again with tap water.

steps.title: Counterstain the Smear
steps.instruction: Apply counter stain (Methylene Blue, Gold Biotechnology Catalog #M-680) and wait for 5 minutes before washing the slide with clean water.

steps.title: Examine Under Microscope
steps.instruction: Thoroughly scan the smear for parasite identification using a compound microscope (e.g., Olympus CH20i) with 40x and 100x (immersion oil) objectives.

steps.title: Final Cleaning and Drying
steps.instruction: Clean the back side of the slide with tissue paper and place it in a draining rack to air dry for 5 minutes.
